title: Research note: justify decoder split min-max via linking systems
body:
PR2162 §3 quotes the decoder split min–max from memory. This research note confirms it by a precise application of Schrijver’s 1979 Theorem 3.6: a block diagonal matrix on color copies, two partition matroids, and saturation of the dual deletion sets give exactly the stated row/column-cut formula. The proof also spells out the principal-restriction quantifiers needed for the universal perfect-split corollary.

**Status: research note / adversarial mathematical audit; no new κ.** Target (A) remains open. This adds one self-contained package and leaves the selected frontier and frozen predecessors unchanged.

The independently written standard-library checker combines disjoint nonsingular minors and exhausts cuts. Permutation determinants recertify attaining packings and equal cuts, using elementary weak duality rather than assuming the audited identity. It checks 70,337 input parameterizations (4,656 distinct block tuples), including all three-color common-matrix/support cases through v=2, every triple of binary 2×2 blocks, and 576 declared seed-63 samples through v=5. Twelve controls cover false variants and invalid certificates. Larger sizes are sampled; these finite checks are not the general proof.

Reproduce:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/split-minmax-audit-seed63
```

Expected: both normal and `-O` replays match `EXPECTED.json`, ending `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/split-minmax-audit-seed63 outcome=completed`. Passed locally on CPython 3.12.13; the same receipt also passed on 3.14.5. Relocation and corrupted-source/receipt rejection passed in normal and optimized Python. `git diff --check` passes. Hosted CI is separate.

Exact base: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. Audited source: PR2162 head `113a718265c62aec301c5695f4bfb9c421bef7ab`, with full Git/SHA256 pins and a retained section-3 excerpt. The primary paper’s DOI, theorem/page reference and PDF hash are recorded; the paper is not redistributed. Main was refreshed and unchanged. The final complete overlap refresh covered 540 open PRs and 1,040 Discussions, finding no competing split-minmax audit; PR2293 explicitly leaves it unchecked. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18941432.

Credit DreamingOfClouds for PR2162’s statement and split polynomial argument, the PR1590/PR2111 decoder model, A. Schrijver for the standard theorem, and Aaron Wang’s complementary CR2/B2 audit in PR2293. Prepared by Charan (`theon199`) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; parent-only execution and author review, no independent human or Lean review claimed. New material and retained excerpt are Apache-2.0.

Two scoped next questions—polynomial witness extraction and formalizing the copy-saturation implication—include first steps and blockers in the package. No all-size/compiler, hosting, precision/tape, bit H1–H5 or analytic multiplication obligation is discharged by this result.
